issue: Can the First Step Act's prospective-only change to § 924(c)'s stacking provision be an extraordinary and compelling reason for a compassionate release sentence reduction, including through U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13(b)(6)?

sides.position: The § 924(c) anti-stacking amendment cannot be an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction, even under U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13(b)(6), because that would give the prospective-only amendment retroactive effect Congress withheld.
cases: United States v. Thacker, 4 F.4th 571 (7th Cir. 2021)
United States v. Andrews, 12 F.4th 255 (3d Cir. 2021)
United States v. Rutherford, 120 F.4th 360 (3d Cir. 2024)
United States v. Austin, 125 F.4th 688 (5th Cir. 2025)
United States v. McCall, 56 F.4th 1048 (6th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Crandall, 25 F.4th 582 (8th Cir. 2022)
United States v. Jenkins, 50 F.4th 1185 (D.C. Cir. 2022)
United States v. Black, No. 24-1191 (7th Cir. 2025)

sides.position: The § 924(c) anti-stacking amendment can be an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction, and the Commission's § 1B1.13(b)(6) policy statement validly allows it, because it does not give the amendment full retroactive effect.
cases: United States v. Ruvalcaba, 26 F.4th 14 (1st Cir. 2022)
United States v. McCoy, 981 F.3d 271 (4th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Chen, 48 F.4th 1092 (9th Cir. 2022)
United States v. McGee, 992 F.3d 1035 (10th Cir. 2021)

this_court: The majority follows Thacker and holds that the § 924(c) anti-stacking amendment cannot be an extraordinary and compelling reason. A separate writing argues that Thacker should yield to the Commission's § 1B1.13(b)(6) and would remand for resentencing consideration.
quote: We recognize Thacker's holding that § 924(c)'s anti-stacking amendment cannot constitute an extraordinary and compelling reason for a sentence reduction is not consensus; the courts of appeals have split on the issue.
cite: United States v. Eural Black, No. 24-1191 (7th Cir. 2025)
